Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

zwiftverse (development version)

Breaking changes

  • Requests now identify as zwiftverse with a link to the repo, rather than as the Zwift mobile app.
  • The package is now read-only: zwift_give_rideon() and the low-level zwift_post() have been removed. zwift_rideons() (reading the Ride Ons on an activity) stays.

New features

  • zwift_status() reads Zwift’s public status page: overall status, per-service components, open and recent incidents, upcoming maintenance. No login needed.
  • zp_analysis() and zp_event_analysis() return the second-by-second power, heart rate and altitude behind ZwiftPower race reports, for one rider or a whole event / pen.
  • zp_segment_standings(): every best effort on a ZwiftPower segment, globally or for one team.
  • Cached responses are also kept in memory for the R session, so repeat hits skip the disk read (options(zwiftverse.cache_memory = FALSE) to turn off).
  • print() on a zwift_auth() handle shows token status without revealing the token or credentials.

Documentation

  • README explains where each credential comes from, including how to ask ZwiftRacing.app for an API key, and acknowledges zpdatafetch and zwift-api-documentation.

Robustness

  • zwift_auth() renews tokens early and times their expiry from when the request was sent, falls back to a password login when Zwift rejects a refresh token, treats refresh_expires_in = 0 as non-expiring, and zwift_get() retries once with a fresh token after an unexpected 401.
  • Error responses with an empty body now report their HTTP status instead of a body-parsing error.
  • An empty response body (ZwiftPower’s “no data”) parses as an empty result.

zwiftverse 0.1.0

  • First version: typed clients for the Zwift game API, ZwiftPower and the ZwiftRacing.app v2 API, returning tibbles; auto-paging Zwift lists and event results / entrants; zp_unflag() for ZwiftPower’s [value, flag] fields; an on-disk TTL cache; offline fixture tests; vignettes race-analysis and climb-prediction.
